paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: you don't have to figure out everything to live well before God. The Teacher watches the wicked get praised at their burial, and he watches righteous men get what the wicked deserve. He calls it futile (Ecclesiastes 8:10, 14). He doesn't pretend life adds up neatly, and neither should you.

But he doesn't throw up his hands, either. He says, "it will go well with those who fear God, who are reverent in His presence" (Ecclesiastes 8:12). That's the anchor. Even when the sentence is slow and the scoreboard looks crooked, the Teacher still knows who to trust, and I'm telling you, that's worth more than a whole shelf of answers!

Then he lands it: even when "the wise man claims to know, he is unable to comprehend" (Ecclesiastes 8:17). That's good news for the worn-out baker staring at the ceiling at 3 a.m. trying to solve the universe. You can put the puzzle down, fear God, and take the joy He hands you in your work and your days (Ecclesiastes 8:15). I spent years in a drawer without answers, and I'm still here laughing, because God had me the whole time.
